# clerk_api_key (Resource)

Manages a Clerk API key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "clerk_api_key" "backend" {
  name        = "Backend API Key"
  description = "Used by the backend service"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the API key.

### Optional

- `claims` (String) JSON string of custom claims for the API key.
- `created_by` (String) Identifier of the entity that created the API key. Set on create only.
- `description` (String) Description of the API key.
- `scopes` (List of String) List of scopes for the API key.
- `seconds_until_expiration` (Number) Number of seconds until the API key expires. Write-only: used on create/update, the API returns an expiration timestamp instead.
- `subject` (String) Subject of the API key.
- `type` (String) Type of the API key. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the API key was created.
- `expiration` (String) Expiration timestamp in RFC3339 format.
- `expired` (Boolean) Whether the API key has expired.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the API key.
- `last_used_at` (String) Timestamp when the API key was last used, in RFC3339 format.
- `revoked` (Boolean) Whether the API key has been revoked.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The API key secret. Write-only: only returned on creation, not on subsequent reads.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the API key was last updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import clerk_api_key.example <api_key_id>
```
